+# Configure local actions for Android devices in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+Android local actions let you configure actions that run directly on managed Android devices when supported device events occur. By pairing triggers with actions, you can make devices respond to events such as a device reboot, a Managed Home Screen sign-in, or a change in the device's power connection.
+
+You can use local actions to launch apps, send broadcasts to apps, initiate a global sign-out, or exit Managed Home Screen from kiosk mode.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An Android device enrolled as a [dedicated device](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-dedicated) or [fully managed device](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-fully-managed).
+- For activity actions, Overlay Permission (`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`) granted before you deploy the policy. For more information, see Overlay permission for foreground app launches.
+
+## Create the profile
+
+To configure local actions, create a device configuration profile using the **Local actions** template.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
+2. Select **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Configuration** > **Create** > **New policy**.
+3. Select the following properties:
+
+    - **Platform**: Select **Android Enterprise**.
+    - **Profile type**: Select **Templates**.
+    - **Template name**: Select **Local actions**.
+4. Select **Create**.
+5. In **Basics**, enter the following properties:
+
+    - **Name**: Enter a descriptive name for the policy.
+    - **Description**: Enter a description for the policy. This setting is optional but recommended.
+    - **Profile type**: Select **Corporate owned devices**.
+6. Select **Next**.
+7. In **Configuration settings**, select **Enter JSON data**.
+8. Paste the completed local actions JSON. Use the settings tables, schema, and examples in this article to build the JSON.
+9. Select **Next**.
+10. In **Scope tags** (optional), assign a scope tag to filter the policy to specific IT groups. Select **Next**.
+11. In **Assignments**, select the device groups that should receive the policy. Select **Next**.
+12. In **Review + create**, review the settings. Select **Create** to save and assign the policy.
+
+Note
+
+Local actions are only supported on an Android device enrolled as a dedicated device or fully managed device.
+
+## Overlay permission for foreground app launches
+
+Activity actions require Overlay Permission (`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`). Without it, foreground app launches might fail silently or behave unexpectedly.
+
+Use OEMConfig to grant Overlay Permission to the Microsoft Intune app package, `com.microsoft.intune`. If Managed Home Screen is installed, also grant the permission to the Managed Home Screen package, `com.microsoft.launcher.enterprise`.
+
+For Samsung, Zebra, Legacy Zebra, and Honeywell devices, see [Configure permissions for Managed Home Screen on Android Enterprise devices](configure-managed-home-screen-permissions-android) for OEMConfig instructions.
+
+For other OEMs, use the OEM's instructions to grant Overlay Permission through OEMConfig. If the OEM doesn't support granting the permission through OEMConfig, grant it manually in the device Settings app.
+
+## Trigger settings
+
+A trigger defines the device event that causes one or more local actions to run.
+
+### Supported triggers
+
+Each trigger represents an event that occurs on the device. A configuration can contain multiple trigger-and-action bundles.
+
+| Trigger | Value | When it fires |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Device reboot | `device_reboot` | After the device completes a reboot and the Intune app is ready. |
+| Managed Home Screen sign-in | `mhs_sign_in` | When a user signs in through Managed Home Screen. |
+| Global sign-out | `global_sign_out` | When global sign-out starts on the device. |
+| Device plugged in | `device_plugged_in` | When the device connects to a power source, such as a charger or dock. |
+| Device unplugged | `device_unplugged` | When the device disconnects from a power source. |
+| Schedule | `schedule` | On the configured day and time. |
+
+Note
+
+The plug-in and unplug triggers are intended for use with Managed Home Screen because they require an actively running app to detect the change. To use these triggers without Managed Home Screen, make sure the Microsoft Intune app is running.
+
+### Schedule trigger properties
+
+If you use the `schedule` trigger, configure both schedule properties.
+
+| Property | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `schedule_days` | A comma-separated list of day names. |
+| `schedule_time` | The time in 24-hour `HH:mm` format. |
+
+Note
+
+Day names aren't case-sensitive. For `schedule_time`, only `:00` and `:30` minute values are supported. The schedule trigger has 30-minute precision and might run a few minutes after the configured time.
+
+## Action settings
+
+An action defines what the device does when its associated trigger fires.
+
+### Supported action types
+
+| Action type | Value | Use |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Activity | `activity` | Launch an activity in an app through an intent. |
+| Broadcast | `broadcast` | Send a broadcast intent to an app. |
+| Direct API | `direct_api` | Run a supported Intune device action directly. |
+
+### Direct API actions
+
+For a direct API action, use one of the following action values.
+
+| Action | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Initiate global sign-out from Managed Home Screen | `mhs_sign_out` |
+| Exit Managed Home Screen from kiosk mode | `exit_mhs_from_kiosk_mode` |
+
+### Activity and broadcast action properties
+
+Configure the properties that apply to the action type.
+
+| Key | Type | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `action_type` | `valueString` | Yes | The action type: `activity`, `broadcast`, or `direct_api`. |
+| `package` | `valueString` | Yes for activity and broadcast intents | The target app package name. |
+| `class` | `valueString` | No | The fully qualified class name of the target component. |
+| `action` | `valueString` | Required for direct API actions; optional for intents | The intent action or supported direct API action to run. |
+| `data_uri` | `valueString` | No | A URI for the intent data. |
+| `mime_type` | `valueString` | No | The MIME type that describes the data format. |
+| `flags` | `valueString` | No | A comma-separated list of supported Android intent flags. |
+| `extras` | `valueBundleArray` | No | Key-value pairs that contain additional data for the receiving app. |
+
+### Extra values
+
+If the receiving app requires extras, add each extra to the `extras` array.
+
+| Key | Type | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `extra_key` | `valueString` | Yes | The key name for the extra. |
+| `extra_value` | `valueString` | Yes | The value for the extra. |
+| `extra_type` | `valueString` | No | The data type. Supported values are `string`, `boolean`, `integer`, `long`, `float`, and `double`. The default is `string`. |
+
+Note
+
+Activity and broadcast actions require an explicit target package. The target app must be installed on the device. Implicit intents are blocked, and an action fails silently if its target package isn't installed.
+
+Note
+
+The `data_uri` property supports the `geo`, `http`, `https`, `mailto`, and `tel` URI schemes. The `flags` property supports `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NO_HISTORY`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_EXCLUDE_FROM_RECENTS`, `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NO_ANIMATION`, and `FLAG_ACTIVITY_REORDER_TO_FRONT`.
+
+Important
+
+Don't configure broadcast intents that target Intune management-critical apps, including Intune, Microsoft Authenticator, Company Portal, and Cloud DPC. These broadcasts are blocked. Activity intents can't target custom classes in Intune management-critical apps. For Microsoft Authenticator, Intune, Managed Home Screen, and Remote Help, you can launch the app's main screen, but you can't target a custom class.
+
+## Local actions JSON schema
+
+Local actions use the Android Enterprise managed configuration format. The top-level key is `com.microsoft.intune.localactions`, and its `valueBundleArray` contains the trigger-and-action bundles.
+
+The complete schema is:
+
+```json
+{
+  "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+  "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+  "managedProperty": [
+    {
+      "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+      "valueBundleArray": [
+        {
+          "managedProperty": [
+            {
+              "key": "trigger",
+              "valueString": ""
+            },
+            {
+              "key": "actions",
+              "valueBundleArray": [
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "activity"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "package",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "class",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "data_uri",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "mime_type",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "flags",
+                      "valueString": ""
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "extras",
+                      "valueBundleArray": [
+                        {
+                          "managedProperty": [
+                            {
+                              "key": "extra_key",
+                              "valueString": ""
+                            },
+                            {
+                              "key": "extra_value",
+                              "valueString": ""
+                            },
+                            {
+                              "key": "extra_type",
+                              "valueString": "string"
+                            }
+                          ]
+                        }
+                      ]
+                    }
+                  ]
+                }
+              ]
+            }
+          ]
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+Replace the empty strings with the values for your trigger and actions. You can omit optional properties that you don't use. For each additional trigger, add another bundle to the top-level `valueBundleArray`.
+
+Note
+
+Actions run in configuration order. You can configure up to five actions for each trigger. If you configure more than five, only the first five run.
+
+## JSON examples
+
+Use these examples as starting points, and replace the example package, class, action, and extra values with values from the app developer.
+
+### Launch an app after device reboot
+
+This example launches the main activity of `com.example.safetyapp` after the device reboots. This activity action requires Overlay Permission.
+
+```json
+{
+  "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+  "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+  "managedProperty": [
+    {
+      "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+      "valueBundleArray": [
+        {
+          "managedProperty": [
+            {
+              "key": "trigger",
+              "valueString": "device_reboot"
+            },
+            {
+              "key": "actions",
+              "valueBundleArray": [
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "activity"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "package",
+                      "valueString": "com.example.safetyapp"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": "android.intent.action.MAIN"
+                    }
+                  ]
+                }
+              ]
+            }
+          ]
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Send a broadcast after global sign-out
+
+This example sends a custom broadcast to an example app after global sign-out.
+
+```json
+{
+     "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+     "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+     "managedProperty": [
+       {
+     "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+     "valueBundleArray": [
+         {
+             "managedProperty": [
+                 {
+                     "key":"trigger",
+                     "valueString": "global_sign_out"
+                 },
+                 {
+                     "key": "actions",
+                     "valueBundleArray": [
+                         {
+                             "managedProperty": [
+                                 {
+                                     "key":"action_type",
+                                     "valueString": "broadcast"
+                                 },
+                                 {
+                                     "key":"package",
+                                     "valueString": "com.contoso.examplePackageName"
+                                 },
+                                 {
+                                     "key":"class",
+                                     "valueString": "com.contoso.example.fullyQualifiedClassName"
+                                 },
+                                 {
+                                     "key":"action",
+                                     "valueString": "com.contoso.example.EXAMPLE_CUSTOM_LOB_ACTION"
+                                 },
+                                 {
+                                     "key": "extras",
+                                     "valueBundleArray": [
+                                         {
+                                             "managedProperty": [
+                                                 {"key": "extra_key",
+     "valueString": "example_extra_key_1"},
+                                                 {"key": "extra_value",
+   "valueString": "example_extra_value_1"},
+                                                 {"key": "extra_type",
+"valueString": "string"}
+                                             ]
+                                         },
+                                         {
+                                             "managedProperty": [
+                                                 {"key": "extra_key",
+    "valueString": "example_extra_key_2"},
+                                                 {"key": "extra_value",
+"valueString": "true"},
+                                                 {"key": "extra_type",
+"valueString": "boolean"}
+                                             ]
+                                         }
+                                     ]
+                                 }
+                             ]
+                         }
+                     ]
+                 }
+             ]
+         }
+     ]
+       }
+     ]
+ }
+```
+
+### Run multiple actions after device reboot
+
+This example launches two apps and sends a broadcast after the device reboots. The activity actions require Overlay Permission.
+
+```json
+{
+  "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+  "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+  "managedProperty": [
+    {
+      "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+      "valueBundleArray": [
+        {
+          "managedProperty": [
+            {
+              "key": "trigger",
+              "valueString": "device_reboot"
+            },
+            {
+              "key": "actions",
+              "valueBundleArray": [
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "activity"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "package",
+                      "valueString": "com.example.app1"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": "android.intent.action.MAIN"
+                    }
+                  ]
+                },
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "activity"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "package",
+                      "valueString": "com.example.app2"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": "android.intent.action.MAIN"
+                    }
+                  ]
+                },
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "broadcast"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "package",
+                      "valueString": "com.example.notifyapp"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": "com.example.notifyapp.DEVICE_READY"
+                    }
+                  ]
+                }
+              ]
+            }
+          ]
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Sign out of Managed Home Screen when docked
+
+This example initiates a Managed Home Screen sign-out when the device connects to a charger or dock.
+
+```json
+{
+  "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+  "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+  "managedProperty": [
+    {
+      "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+      "valueBundleArray": [
+        {
+          "managedProperty": [
+            {
+              "key": "trigger",
+              "valueString": "device_plugged_in"
+            },
+            {
+              "key": "actions",
+              "valueBundleArray": [
+                {
+                  "managedProperty": [
+                    {
+                      "key": "action_type",
+                      "valueString": "direct_api"
+                    },
+                    {
+                      "key": "action",
+                      "valueString": "mhs_sign_out"
+                    }
+                  ]
+                }
+              ]
+            }
+          ]
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Launch an app on a schedule
+
+This example launches a safety check-in app at 6:00 AM every weekday. This activity action requires Overlay Permission.
+
+```json
+{
+    "kind": "androidenterprise#managedConfiguration",
+    "productId": "app:com.microsoft.intune",
+    "managedProperty": [
+        {
+            "key": "com.microsoft.intune.localactions",
+            "valueBundleArray": [
+                {
+                    "managedProperty": [
+                        {
+                           "key": "trigger",
+                            "valueString": "schedule"
+                        },
+                        {
+                            "key": "schedule_time",
+                            "valueString": "06:00"
+                        },
+                        {
+                            "key": "schedule_days",
+    "valueString": "monday,tuesday,wednesday,thursday,friday"
+                        },
+                        {
+                            "key": "actions",
+                            "valueBundleArray": [
+                                {
+                                    "managedProperty": [
+                                        {
+                                            "key": "action_type",
+                                            "valueString": "activity"
+                                        },
+                                        {
+                                            "key": "package",
+                                            "valueString":"com.contoso.safetycheck"
+                                        },
+                                        {
+                                            "key": "action",
+"valueString":"android.intent.action.MAIN"
+                                        }
+                                    ]
+                                }
+                            ]
+                        }
+                    ]
+                }
+            ]
+        }
+    ]
+}
+```

+# Configure maintenance windows for Windows updates in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+Use maintenance windows in Microsoft Intune to control when automatic Windows Update actions can begin on managed devices. You can restrict downloads, installations, and update-related restarts to a scheduled period.
+
+Maintenance windows help you plan updates for devices that need to remain available during operating hours, such as kiosks, shared devices, and manufacturing equipment. Configure a one-time window or a recurring daily, weekly, or monthly schedule.
+
+Maintenance windows govern Windows Update content, including quality updates, feature updates, Hotpatch updates, .NET updates, drivers, and firmware. They don't determine which updates are approved or offered to a device.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Before you create a policy:
+
+- Confirm that devices are enrolled in Intune and run a supported Windows version. The underlying maintenance window settings require Windows 11, version 24H2 with KB5077181, build 26100.7840, or later.
+- Confirm that you have Intune permissions to create, configure, and assign device configuration policies.
+- Identify a device group for your initial deployment. Test the policy on representative devices before assigning it more broadly.
+- Review the update policies assigned to those devices, including deferrals, deadlines, grace periods, and expedited updates.
+
+For the underlying Windows settings and operating system requirements, see [Update Policy CSP](/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-update).
+
+## How maintenance windows work
+
+A maintenance window controls when the automatic update actions you select can begin. Actions that aren't selected continue to follow other applicable Windows Update policies.
+
+| Update action | Actions restricted to the maintenance window | Actions that can occur outside the window |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Download, install and restart | Download, installation, and update-related restart | None of these automatic actions, except where another policy or event takes priority |
+| Install and restart | Installation and update-related restart | Download |
+| Restart only | Update-related restart | Download and installation |
+
+All maintenance window times use the device's local time. For example, a window that starts at 23:00 starts at 11:00 PM in each device's local time zone.
+
+An action that begins during the window can continue after the window ends. A maintenance window doesn't guarantee that all update work finishes before the end of the scheduled period.
+
+Maintenance windows control automatic update actions. Users can still initiate update actions outside the window when the Windows experience and other applicable policies allow them.
+
+## Create a maintenance window policy
+
+### 1. Create the policy
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Intune admin center.
+2. Select **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Maintenance windows**.
+3. Select **Create policy**.
+4. On **Basics**, enter a descriptive **Name** and an optional **Description**.
+5. Select **Next**.
+
+For example, use the name **Weekly kiosk maintenance** and describe the devices and approved maintenance period.
+
+### 2. Choose the update actions
+
+On **Configuration settings**, expand **Maintenance Windows** and configure these settings:
+
+1. For **Workload type**, select **Updates**.
+2. Set **Enable Maintenance windows** to **On**.
+3. For **Update action**, select one of the following options:
+    - **Download, install and restart**
+    - **Install and restart**
+    - **Restart only**
+
+Choose the option that matches the activities you need to restrict. For example, select **Install and restart** if devices can download updates during operating hours but must wait until the maintenance period to install them and restart.
+
+### 3. Configure the schedule
+
+Configure the schedule settings in the order shown in the admin center:
+
+1. **Repeat schedule**
+2. Schedule-specific options, when applicable
+3. **Start date**
+4. **Duration (hours)**
+5. **Start time**
+
+Enter the start date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format and the start time in `HH:MM` format. The duration must be from 2 through 24 hours.
+
+The admin center requires a start date. Windows uses that date for a non-repeating window. For recurring windows, Windows starts on the earliest date that matches the configured schedule.
+
+#### One-time window
+
+To configure a single maintenance period:
+
+1. Set **Repeat schedule** to **None**.
+2. Enter the **Start date**.
+3. Enter the **Duration (hours)**.
+4. Enter the **Start time** in device-local time.
+
+Keep one-time schedules current. After the scheduled period passes, update the date or remove the one-time configuration as appropriate.
+
+#### Daily window
+
+To configure a maintenance period every day:
+
+1. Set **Repeat schedule** to **Daily**.
+2. Complete **Start date**.
+3. Enter the **Duration (hours)** and **Start time**.
+
+No weekday or monthly selections are required.
+
+#### Weekly window
+
+To configure a maintenance period on selected days:
+
+1. Set **Repeat schedule** to **Weekly**.
+2. Under **Weekly – Day selection**, select one or more days.
+3. Complete **Start date**.
+4. Enter the **Duration (hours)** and **Start time**.
+
+The window occurs on each selected day.
+
+#### Monthly window
+
+Set **Repeat schedule** to **Monthly**, and then configure **Monthly – Schedule type**.
+
+For a day-based schedule:
+
+1. Select **Day-based**.
+2. Set **Day of month** to a value from 1 through 28.
+3. Complete **Start date**, **Duration (hours)**, and **Start time**.
+
+For a week-based schedule:
+
+1. Select **Week-based**.
+2. Choose **Week in Month**: **First**, **Second**, **Third**, **Fourth**, or **Last**.
+3. Choose **Day of the week**.
+4. Complete **Start date**, **Duration (hours)**, and **Start time**.
+
+For example, a week-based schedule can run on the second Tuesday or last Sunday of each month.
+
+After you configure the schedule, select **Next**.
+
+### 4. Assign and create the policy
+
+1. On **Scope tags**, add the scope tags your organization uses to control administrative access, and then select **Next**.
+2. On **Assignments**, select the groups that receive the policy. Add exclusions if needed, and then select **Next**.
+3. On **Review + create**, review the update action, schedule, scope tags, and assignments.
+4. Select **Create**.
+
+## Example: Weekly overnight maintenance
+
+An organization allows kiosks to download updates during operating hours but wants installation and update-related restarts to begin during an overnight maintenance period.
+
+Configure the policy as follows:
+
+| Setting | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Workload type | Updates |
+| Enable Maintenance windows | On |
+| Update action | Install and restart |
+| Repeat schedule | Weekly |
+| Weekly – Day selection | Sunday |
+| Duration (hours) | 4 |
+| Start time | 23:00 |
+
+Complete the required **Start date** field. For this recurring schedule, Windows uses the selected weekday and start time rather than the start date to determine the next window.
+
+The window starts every Sunday at 11:00 PM in each device's local time and ends Monday at 3:00 AM. Downloads can occur outside the window. Installation or restart work that begins during the window can continue after it ends.
+
+## Monitor the policy and validate update behavior
+
+To review policy deployment:
+
+1. Select **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Maintenance windows**.
+2. Select the policy.
+3. Review **Device and user check-in status**, **Device assignment status**, and **Per setting status**.
+4. Investigate errors, conflicts, and devices that haven't received the policy.
+
+Per-setting reports can show the underlying Windows policy settings separately. For example, a weekly schedule can appear as separate settings for individual days of the week.
+
+Policy deployment status shows whether the configuration reached the device. It doesn't, by itself, confirm that an update installed or a restart occurred during the window.
+
+Use your existing Windows Update or Windows Autopatch reporting to validate update behavior. Compare installation and restart timestamps with the configured schedule, accounting for each device's local time zone.
+
+## Interactions with other update policies
+
+Maintenance windows work alongside other Windows Update policies. Review these interactions when you plan a deployment.
+
+### Policies and events that can take priority
+
+The following policies or events can allow update actions outside the maintenance window:
+
+| Policy or event | Effect |
+| --- | --- |
+| Expedited quality updates | An expedited deployment can take priority over the maintenance window. |
+| Expired deadlines and grace periods | Windows can enforce the update and required restart outside the window after the applicable deadline and grace period expire. |
+| Device provisioning | Required update or setup actions during provisioning can take priority over maintenance window restrictions. |
+| Education cart servicing policy | This specialized servicing policy can take priority when configured. |
+| Minor-impact updates | Updates classified by Windows as minor impact can occur outside the window. |
+
+### Deferrals affect update availability
+
+Deferrals control when an update is offered to a device. They don't create an alternative maintenance window.
+
+If an update is still deferred when a window occurs, it isn't available for that window. After the deferral expires and the update is offered, the selected automatic actions can begin during a subsequent applicable window.
+
+For example, a device with a seven-day quality update deferral and a Saturday maintenance window might not process a Tuesday release during the first Saturday window.
+
+### Other scheduling settings
+
+For actions governed by a maintenance window, active hours and other update scheduling settings don't provide an alternative period for those actions to begin.
+
+Review the complete update configuration rather than treating the maintenance window as a replacement for update approval, availability, or deadline policies.
+
+## Troubleshoot unexpected behavior
+
+### Update activity occurs outside the window
+
+Check whether:
+
+- The activity is included in **Update action**. For example, **Restart only** doesn't restrict downloads or installations.
+- The action began during the window and continued after it ended.
+- A user initiated the action.
+- An expedited update, expired deadline, or another higher-priority event applied.
+- You compared the event time with the device's local time.
+
+### An update doesn't install or the device doesn't restart
+
+Check whether:
+
+- The policy successfully reached the device.
+- An applicable update is available and is no longer deferred.
+- A restart is required.
+- The device is powered on and available.
+- Required download and installation work has completed.
+- The schedule matches the device's local time.
+- A one-time window has already passed.
+- The window provides enough time for the selected actions.
+
+### A recurring window doesn't run when expected
+
+Check the recurrence and schedule-specific settings:
+
+- For a weekly schedule, select at least one day.
+- For a monthly day-based schedule, use a day from 1 through 28.
+- For a monthly week-based schedule, configure both the week and weekday.
+- Confirm that the device received the policy and uses the expected local date and time.
